title: D-Wave Reports Its Q2 2026 Financial Results Showing Bookings Surge, Technical Progress, and Quantum Circuits Acquisition Impact - Quantum Computing Report
gist: D-Wave Quantum's Q2 2026 revenue was flat year-over-year at $3.1 million on system-sale timing, but first-half bookings surged over 1,120% to $35.5 million and remaining performance obligations rose 668% to $40.7 million, shifting the story from revenue to backlog. Alongside, D-Wave laid out a dual-platform roadmap — 20,000 annealing qubits by 2029 and 100,000 by 2031, plus gate-model milestones running from 17 physical qubits in 2026 to a 100-logical-qubit machine in 2032 — while cash fell to $546.2 million after the Quantum Circuits acquisition.

insights.claim: D-Wave Quantum's Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million, flat versus $3.1 million in Q2 2025 and up 6.9% from $2.9 million in Q1 2026, with the report attributing the flatness to system sale timing.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Lumpy system-sale timing makes quarterly revenue a poor read on D-Wave's trajectory; bookings are the signal to track instead.
insights.locator: Opening paragraph — "While quarterly revenue remained flat due to system sale timing"

insights.claim: D-Wave's first-half 2026 bookings rose more than 1,120% year-over-year to $35.5 million, anchored by a single new $20 million system sale plus $2.3 million contributed by the Quantum Circuits, Inc. acquisition.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: More than half the bookings growth comes from one $20M system sale — concentration risk means the growth rate is unlikely to repeat linearly.
insights.quote: First-half bookings surged over 1,120% year-over-year to $35.5 million, anchored by a new $20 million system sale and $2.3 million contributed from the acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc.

insights.claim: D-Wave's Remaining Performance Obligations jumped 668% to $40.7 million, of which 57% is expected to convert into recognized revenue over the next 12 months.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: 57% of $40.7M implies roughly $23M of contracted revenue over the coming year against a ~$3M quarterly run-rate — a step-change if it converts on schedule.
insights.locator: Financial Performance & Commercial Expansion — "As a result, Remaining Performance Obligations"

themes.theme: Mix shift from pilots to production

insights.claim: Commercial customers generated 67.7% of D-Wave's first-half 2026 revenue, up from 16.0% in H1 2025, with Forbes Global 2000 clients accounting for nearly half of total revenue.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: A jump from 16% to 68% commercial revenue is the strongest evidence yet that D-Wave's base is corporate rather than grant-funded.
insights.locator: Financial Performance & Commercial Expansion — "Commercial adoption continues to shift"

insights.claim: Production applications now account for 37.3% of D-Wave's Quantum Computing as a Service (QCaaS) revenue, indicating a move beyond experimental pilots.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Production share of QCaaS is the recurring-revenue quality metric — rising share implies stickier, renewable contracts.
insights.locator: Financial Performance & Commercial Expansion — "Production applications now represent"

insights.claim: D-Wave logged enterprise customer wins including AT&T, Nasdaq Verafin, Unisys, Shionogi, Oki Electric and an unnamed major entertainment brand.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: The named logos span telecom, financial crime, IT services and pharma — breadth suggests annealing optimization is finding multiple verticals.
insights.locator: "The quarter also brought additional government funding"

insights.claim: D-Wave's Q2 2026 net loss narrowed to $48.0 million from $167.3 million a year earlier, a 71.3% improvement the report attributes largely to reduced non-cash warrant liability charges rather than operations.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: The loss improvement is an accounting artifact — operating loss actually doubled year-over-year, so don't read narrowing net loss as progress toward breakeven.
insights.quote: Net loss narrowed significantly to $48.0 million for the quarter, largely due to reduced non-cash warrant liability charges

insights.claim: D-Wave's Q2 2026 operating expenses of $55.0 million were up 93.0% year-over-year against $3.1 million of revenue, producing a $53.3 million operating loss, more than double the $26.5 million loss of Q2 2025.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Opex is roughly 18x revenue; the company is spending far ahead of the P&L, so backlog conversion timing determines financing need.

insights.claim: D-Wave ended Q2 2026 with $546.2 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments, down 7.2% sequentially and 33.3% from $819.3 million a year earlier, after funding the Quantum Circuits transaction.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: A third of the cash pile is gone year-over-year; at the current operating loss the runway is finite enough to make equity issuance a live risk.
insights.locator: Financial Performance & Commercial Expansion — "D-Wave closed the period with $546.2 million"

insights.claim: D-Wave's Advantage3 annealing roadmap uses a multi-chip fabric with superconducting interconnects to scale past single-chip limits, targeting 20,000 qubits by 2029 and 100,000 qubits by 2031.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Multi-chip interconnect is the specific engineering risk to monitor — if it works, annealing qubit counts scale an order of magnitude ahead of gate-model machines.
insights.locator: Dual-Platform Hardware & Software Roadmaps — "For its Advantage3™ annealing track"

insights.claim: D-Wave published peer-reviewed research in Nature on a high-fidelity two-qubit gate built on a dual-rail superconducting architecture that reduces hardware overhead for fault tolerance.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Lower physical-to-logical overhead is the single biggest cost lever in fault-tolerant quantum; peer review makes the claim harder to dismiss as marketing.
insights.locator: Dual-Platform Hardware & Software Roadmaps — "In gate-model quantum computing"

insights.claim: D-Wave set explicit gate-model milestones of 17 physical qubits in 2026, 181 physical qubits by 2028, 10 logical qubits by 2030, and a 100-logical-qubit system capable of over one million operations by 2032.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Dated, falsifiable milestones give a checklist to score D-Wave's gate-model credibility against IBM/Google-style roadmaps.
insights.quote: targeting 17 physical qubits in 2026, 181 physical qubits by 2028, 10 logical qubits by 2030, and a 100-logical-qubit system capable of over one million operations by 2032

insights.claim: D-Wave is pursuing both annealing and gate-model architectures simultaneously and announced an upcoming error-aware simulator to help developers build error-resilient algorithms.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: A dual-platform strategy hedges architecture risk but splits R&D spend — it partly explains the 93% year-over-year opex increase.
insights.locator: Dual-Platform Hardware & Software Roadmaps — "On the technical front"

insights.claim: D-Wave secured a $1.57 million NSF grant under the NQVL ERASE project and second-year defense funding via NORDTECH during the quarter.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Non-dilutive government funding is small in absolute terms but signals continued federal validation of the annealing/gate programs.
insights.locator: "The quarter also brought additional government funding"
